title: Fix: up-button tap from live bottom didn't visibly scroll (preserveScrollTop anchored at bottom)
action: User field-test finding (2026-07-27, mobile+desktop): tapping nudge-up flickered but never visibly scrolled; desktop native PageUp key did scroll. Root cause: applyScreen()'s preserveScrollTop keeps the same distance-from-bottom across a content swap -- the drag-scroll-to-top trigger works because the real scroll already happened before loadOlder() fires, but a button tap usually starts from the live bottom (distance ~0), so the freshly-expanded history lands right back at the bottom (a full re-render, no visible movement). Fix: nudge-up's click handler now consumes historyArmed (false) before calling loadOlder(), then explicitly jumps viewport.scrollTop to 0 once it resolves -- mirroring nudge-down's explicit jump to scrollHeight -- so the programmatic scroll doesn't re-arm a duplicate history fetch via the drag-scroll listener.

truths: tapping nudge-up from the live bottom moves scrollTop to 0 (visibly reveals history), not just re-renders in place
the resulting programmatic scroll does not trigger a second, redundant history fetch

artifacts.substantive: nudge-up handler clears historyArmed and jumps scrollTop to 0 after loadOlder() resolves
regression test: tap from live bottom asserts scrollTop===0 and exactly one history fetch even after a simulated scroll event

key_links: nudge-up handler still calls the same loadOlder() as the drag-scroll trigger (D3), only the post-load scroll position changed
prohibitions: no change to nudge-down's existing behavior
